Params: Tactical Training Course, Holo-Combat Training Grounds
In the narrow prep corridor, the blue-haired girl moves forward with her weapon raised. The white-haired girl follows in silence, a deliberate five meters of distance between them.
Five meters is too far for clear communication and just barely close enough for mutual cover.
Adelyde opens her mouth, but the words do not come.
All the questions she had rehearsed—where she had gone, why she left without a word... they all lodge in her throat the moment she tries to speak.
The corridor is silent. Five meters apart, and between them is the weight of a whole world.
This time, she raises her voice.
Thirty seconds to sim battle. Keep the line clear for tactical communication.
The words come out hard and flat, without a trace of give.
Alright, everyone's here. Today's sim has one goal: capture and hold.

A holographic display opens before them, revealing a central control tower at the heart of a violent storm. Rain lashes against its sides, and fog curls around its base, isolating it from everything else.
Take the central control tower and hold it for 120 seconds. Enemy AI forces will hit you in waves that get worse the longer you stay. If the timer stops even once, it's a loss.
Remember, taking the tower is just step one. Holding it is what wins.
Knockdowns, covering fire, or any other effective tactical actions all earn you tactical points. But they only count if you win. Lose, and they all go to zero.
Also, we're piloting a new role system for this exercise and the upcoming competition. Three positions: assault, fire support, and tactical coordinator.
Role indicators appear in everyone's field of view. Adelyde is slotted as assault, Arakna as fire support, and the third member as tactical coordinator.
Move to your positions. Operation begins.

The scene shifts in an instant. Spray carries the scent of the sea, and the sound of waves fills their ears. The holographic port is rendered with painstaking detail, down to the rust on the crane arms.
She knows this kind of place inside out. She knows which way the container shadows fall and exactly where a patrol line breaks between the gaps.
The blue-haired girl moves past her and heads straight for the control tower.
We fight separately. Scores will prove who gets to make the calls.
What?? Wait, what about me?! I'm the tactical coordinator, and who am I even coordinating?! You two—HEY!
He receives no reply. The two figures break left and right, disappearing into the shadows of the containers.
The push turns into a race.

From the left flank, shots land with metronomic precision, sentinel drones dropping half a second before their alarms can sound. From the right, suppressing fire tears through the defensive line, rolling up the patrols one position after another.
In the corner of their vision, the training system updates her score silently. Adelyde is in the lead.
The next update shows Arakna overtaking her.
They push forward without a word, moving fast enough to leave no opening for the enemy and no room to steal each other's kills.
From the observation deck, Wells watches with crossed arms as two kill counters climb in a wild race, while a single tactical coordinator dot crawls across the map at a snail's pace.
At the rear of the battlefield, a disheveled figure sprints forward, gasping out words between ragged breaths.
Hey! P-please slow down, both of you! If you keep making this much noise, you're going to draw—
An alarm shrieks from somewhere in the port. The lights flash red, and a storm of gunfire pours down without warning.
Deep in the container maze ahead, heavy machinery roars to life. At the far end of their view, a wall of muzzle flashes lights up the darkness.
A probing shot sends the container between them flying. Both figures dive into the same maintenance hatch at almost the same moment.
The tunnel stretches ahead, pipes running deep into the port. Gunfire thuds overhead, muffled and heavy, a single steel plate away.
Searchlights pass across the grating in measured sweeps, each beam catching two faces that refuse to back down.
This is the closest cover to the front. You're here for the same reason I am.
Don't put me in the same box as you.
Both of them know the truth: the firepower level has escalated, the port has deployed new horrifying defenses, and the way forward holds nothing but the unknown.
But neither of them will say it.
What made you stop, princess? You are still ahead. Not looking to widen the gap?
In silence, Adelyde lowers herself against the pipe and begins her routine checks. Magazines, ammunition, exoskeleton thrusters... Every motion smooth and rehearsed.
Enemy firepower just spiked, you've got no intel on what's ahead, and you're still planning to rush in solo?
Two years ago you pulled the same thing, kept everything inside, carried it all yourself. How'd that turn out?
I got used to it after you all left.
I just don't want to drag anyone else down.
Spare me the self-sacrificing hero speech. What, you want to die before me that badly?
Let's get one thing straight, Ade... Helio. If we lose this thing, or if one of us bites it, don't expect anyone to be around to take your apology.
The shout ricochets through the pipe, and Adelyde's hands pause mid-load.
Then the hatch above crashes open, and a figure tumbles down, landing with a heavy thud in the space between them.
Ha... ha... finally caught up to you...
Please, both of you, just stop fighting!
The young man lifts his hands in surrender, his voice cracking without a hint of shame.
Hey, blue hair, you look super familiar. Didn't we meet at the auditorium?
Say what you need to say or get in line and keep quiet.
I-I-I'm Aristo from the Transatlantic Economic Community, and yeah, the one at the very bottom of this course's rankings.
Two pairs of eyes cut toward him, cold and pointed.
Oh... "Aristo the Misplaced Talent." They also call you "Mr. Stay Alive." I remember you. You've got perfect scores in theory, culture, and every science-related course...
Hehe, well, before my mom shipped me off here for "real experience," my grades were—
And failed every combat course. You're retaking this one for the second time.
Ouch, you don't have to rub it in... Look, this is my last chance. If I fail again, I get kicked out. Please, both of you, give me a chance—
The young man presses his palms together, face twisted in a pitiful grimace, shaking them in a desperate plea.
A-anyway, don't go forward! We need to go another way!
...And what makes you so sure about that?
Aristo lifts his terminal with shaking hands.
On the screen, six drone feeds are arranged in a clean grid, each one showing the new defensive line ahead from a different angle.
I-I'm way too scared of dying... I didn't dare walk on my own. I sent every recon drone I had out ahead...
Adelyde and Arakna exchange a glance, then speak at the same time.
Talk. What are we looking at?
He spreads the terminal's projection across the floor, swiping through each drone feed. The moment his focus turns to the screens rather than the people around him, something in his eyes changes.

Two new phase turrets covering the tower's front, overlapping fields, no dead zones. East side looks mined. West side, an ambush squad in the container corridor. Heat signatures show... nine hostiles, heavily armed.
Worst part is the tower top. The mobile cannons there track by sound... which means, the first shot gets locked instantly.
This is... the hardest sim I've ever faced.
The space falls silent. Arakna folds her arms and casts a sharp sideways look at Adelyde.
Double firepower, no blind spots. Still feeling brave enough to go solo?
Solo odds are zero. We have to work together.
The sharp mockery dies on her lips. The look Arakna gives Adelyde now carries a mix of confusion and faint resentment.
Adelyde is already crouched over the projection, her fingers moving swiftly through the gaps in the defensive grid.

Arakna, I need you to take the north exit from this corridor and lay down suppressing fire on the west container zone. You've got cover and firepower. Help me draw the cannons and the ambush squad in.

Aristo, split your drones into two groups. One group scouts Arakna's route, the other triggers the east minefield's edge for a second feint. Then take this pipeline to the tower's maintenance level and hold there for my signal.
Th-the front?! Straight into both phase turrets?!
Overlapping fire means synchronized charge. How long's the window?
Plenty. The exoskeleton's fast enough to get me through.
The plan is laid out. The pipe falls quiet. Adelyde looks up, her gaze moving across both teammates before it comes to rest on Arakna.
Arakna, you'll be holding the heaviest fire for twenty seconds. I need you on this.
Ha... twenty seconds. Fine. You've got it.
She hefts her gun onto her shoulder and looks away, then notices Adelyde frozen in place.
Make it quick. We talk after we win.
At the end of the corridor, a service door marks the way to the front. Three figures, streaked with dust and grime, stop before it.
(Production Note by Runlin: Here we can have the door open, then fade to black and transition to the observation deck.)
On the observation deck, Wells watches the surveillance feed. Three minutes of stillness, and then the battlefield erupts.
Suppressing fire rakes the western flank. The eastern mines blow in sequence. The defenders split their reinforcements, scrambling to cover two major attack areas that hold no one.
(Production Note by Runlin: Here we can cut to the control tower background, add a full-screen comms effect, and just show the text.)
With all guns turned away, a blur slips through the gap between phase turrets and enters the tower.
The scatter fire pulls back to a defensive posture. The drone swarm fans out around the tower, reporting each approaching defender wave with surgical clarity.
[Squad Seven: Mission Complete. Overall Rating: S]
[Squad Seven: Mission Complete. Overall Rating: S]
The young instructor creates a new memo on his terminal, types half a line, then locks the screen. The three cadets return to the classroom from the simulation.
Solid tactics, clean execution. Last S rating was four years ago.
Whoa, whoa! I passed? And I got an S?!
That's for the second half. Let's talk about the first.
His gaze rests on each girl for a second, his face stern.
Adelyde. Arakna. Eight minutes in, one of you had twelve kills, the other eleven.
But there were only three transmissions on tactical comms total. Not one of them constituted effective coordination. No teamwork at all.
I don't care what's going on between you two. Zero coordination, zero communication, that's not just bad teamwork. That's throwing away lives and disregarding the importance of combat tactics.
Formal warning for both of you.
Remember, the battlefield doesn't forgive failure. Neither do your own lives.
You're the only one who remembered your role from start to finish. Recon: flawless. Intel handoff: flawless.
Next time, level your breathing when you're discussing tactics. Your team doesn't need to hear how scared you are.
Yes, sir... Wait, was that a compliment?
Squad Seven's results will be recorded as competition entry references.
The debriefing ends without a single mention of what a Helio deserves or how a member of a TEC family should be handled.
His words are sharp and unsparing, and yet Adelyde feels relief. In front of this instructor, she is simply a student.
For once, the crest on her chest does not press down on her shoulders.
Adelyde stops. A few paces away, the blue-haired girl stands with her arms folded, her gaze directed elsewhere.
Some of what I said earlier... I went too far. Just forget it.
But I wasn't lying about not wanting my teammates to die for nothing.
She turns and walks away without a moment's hesitation.
Where have you been these two years? Why did you never come back? I tried reaching you so many times... no one ever answered.
...Are you playing dumb, or do you really not know?
By the time Arakna has finished laying everything out, evening has already arrived.
What are you going to do?
You're starting to sound exactly like them.
Once I graduate, I'm going back. I'll take over the family's business from within.
And when I do—every list, every deal, every forced relocation—I'll tear them down one by one... I'll bring everyone back.
What proof do I have that you won't become one of them?
That's impossible. You know who I—
I can't bet on that anymore, Adelyde Helio. We can fight together. Our teamwork is flawless.
But you and your family? That's where I draw the line.
Adelyde's throat goes dry. Many things flood her mind: the dock, the airship, the Wishing Platform, the bouquet of Bourbon roses, and the apology she never managed to speak.
Once, there were so many words they could share. Now there is nothing but a whole ocean of silence stretching between her and Arakna.
She forces the words past her lips, and they come out rough and broken.
On her way back to the dorms after training, Adelyde finds herself at that familiar vantage point again. From here, she can just make out a corner of the square.
Beneath the student activity banner, a familiar blue-haired figure steps into the center of the crowd. Through the prism, light breaks across her face in sharp angles.
She raises a small terminal and a megaphone and begins to speak.
Arakna Sorano here, checking in for all of you who follow the Voice of the Planet newspaper. Our source is safe, and we've got new information.
A few days ago, a student vote was held on whether to allow a Transatlantic Economic Community research foundation to partner with on-campus research clubs.
We have reason to believe they're hiding something.
(Production Note by Runlin: For Student 1/2/3's portraits, use shaded ones of F.O.S. students.)
Arakna projects the foundation's report, along with several compliance and background check documents. The students in the back rise on their toes, straining to see.
Any foundation seeking campus partnerships should be transparent about funding sources, conflicts of interest, and IP ownership.

But the gaps in this report show they're trying to disguise the real nature of the money. The foundation is tax-exempt, and several sponsors are hidden behind layers of anonymity, with the original donors completely obscured.
With assistance from some legally minded students on campus, we traced its largest funding streams and the labs they're tied to.
She raises her hand, and the terminal casts a list of names into the air above the square. One is magnified to a scale that leaves no room for evasion.
Wait, the same Kurono that had three research licenses pulled last year?
Yes, that Kurono. M.I.N.D. technology, gene editing, digital life, human augmentation, and all that "anonymous" lab equipment you've been using are all from them.
Are you playing dumb, or do you really not know?
Arakna's lips curled into a cold smile as she turned to look at Adelyde. But the sharp retort she was waiting for never comes. The white-haired girl's eyes held only sincerity and pain.
So you really don't know. They kept you well "protected."
The night of the Purge, they pulled my Atlantic Eye enrollment, canceled my housing lease, killed all my access, and my comms went dead with it.
The "family's" solution is the South Atlantic. They called it a "Human Resource Reallocation Program," voluntary, with transport and basic needs covered.
I grew up in an orphanage. I had no say. None of us tied to the Copperfields did.
...And then? What happened in the South Atlantic?
I worked at an alloy parts factory owned by the Transatlantic Economic Community. Pipes, valves, and other components for the Atlantic Eye. Alkali wash station. Paid by the piece.
Three months of that, and your hands stop looking like hands.
She shook her hands with a rueful laugh. There was sorrow in her eyes, and something else Adelyde could not quite place.

Her mind struggled to fit the memory of that carefree, radiant girl with the image of someone laboring on an assembly line. But Arakna's face lit up with a bright smile, as if she were recalling something tender and warm.
Why do you look more miserable than I do? Back then, none of us gave up.

We kept each other going. At least we wouldn't starve to death. Worked through storms and sun, even learned to weave through the local gang firefights like it was part of the job. Call it a field trip, if you want.
Because we all believed it was temporary. That eventually, we'd make it back to the Atlantic Eye.
At that, the smile faded from Arakna's face.
Yes, that Kurono. M.I.N.D. technology, gene editing, digital life, human augmentation, and all that "anonymous" lab equipment you've been using are all from them.
Now, on to the second item.
The projection switches. Rows of obscured identification numbers flash up on the screen.
While I was in the South Atlantic, we were regularly supplying parts to Transatlantic Economic Community companies. And every now and then, I'd come across things I wasn't meant to see.
South Atlantic shipping lane, Cargo Fleet No. 7. Run by a Kurono logistics subsidiary.
The paperwork said medical supplies and humanitarian transfers. But I cross-checked those numbers. I pulled records from three different South Atlantic jurisdictions—
They matched the inmate codes for death row prisoners.
One-way trips, no return. Where were they sent? For what purpose? And why was the funding tagged as humanitarian?
Someone had to have asked these questions. So where are they now?
Because we all believed it was temporary. That eventually, we'd make it back to the Atlantic Eye.
I found emails sent by the family about a year ago, something like an amnesty.
Heh... So you're not completely in the dark.
But here's what you don't know: that email actually made me defend them.
They made it clear in the email. To come back to the Atlantic Eye, we had to sign an NDA. So I tried to bring everyone around, the ones still holding onto their doubts.

The Atlantic Eye was built by the four families... They gave us that platform, that's just the truth. And on it, people from everywhere, from every background, once worked side by side for one goal without a single wall between them.

I told them, they're not seeing the full picture. An operation that massive has to have reasons we're not aware of. Once the review is over, someone will come for us. The innocent don't get locked out forever.
Arakna's laughter carried an edge of bitter cold, almost painful.
Not only did no one come back, but more people got sent to the South Atlantic.
The NDA required full disclosure of all personal ties. Family, teachers, collaborators, financial connections... everything, to prove there were no hidden links to Copperfield's core.
And then came the second round. People we named, people who were never on any list, their accounts frozen, their jobs stripped, shipped here with the rest of us.
After that, I holed up in a tiny room, too ashamed to face the sun, too ashamed to face anyone. I even thought about just ending it.
She dismisses the projection and faces the crowd, the sharp light from the prism flickering around her.
Third thing, and this one I have to finish.
Two years ago, the Transatlantic Economic Community went public with its position as Kurono's largest shareholder and began rolling out formal cooperation.
Almost simultaneously, the Copperfield family was investigated for alleged major violations. And just like that, the Transatlantic Economic Community was down to three families.
We may never know the full story, but what we do know is that numerous innocent people got swept up in it.

The Copperfields never asked where you came from. If you had the skill, you had a place, even in their most classified projects. And that's exactly why, when the Purge hit two years ago, these people were the first to be discarded.

The technicians connected to the Copperfields were reassigned to factories in the South Atlantic. Piece by piece, the Atlantic Eye's systems passed through our hands, each one feeding the city at her heart, the city we would never be allowed to enter again.
I was one of them. I was sixteen.
After that, I holed up in a tiny room, too ashamed to face the sun, too ashamed to face anyone. I even thought about just ending it.
But they never blamed me. They even scraped together whatever little they had and gave it all to me.
They told me to quit the factory and go back to school.
On that assembly line, we had ocean current modelers, bionic engineers, PhDs with prize-winning papers... the finest minds of the Golden Age, turning screws so I could go to school.
They said their Atlantic Eye projects were gone. But they had a new one. Me.
They said I was the most gifted child they'd ever known.
That's why I'm standing here today.
Out of everyone on that line, I was the only one who made it into this academy.
Only I have a place where I can still be heard.
She draws a long breath and steadies the rising tide of emotions within her.
I'm not saying this for your pity, or even to make you feel what I felt. I'm just showing you the cost when you swallow the dream someone feeds you without question.
We ask why of the stars, the oceans, the deepest unknowns. Don't forget to ask why of the people.
I'm not telling you to distrust everyone. I'm telling you that the gold of the Golden Age should be measured in people, not in what they achieve.
Look at a masterpiece on canvas: the colors, the emotions. It's breathtaking, yes. But are there splinters left in the frame? And did the artist ever get the recognition and reward they deserved?
Please, think carefully before you cast your vote. No matter how sweet the deal looks, keep your eyes open.
Because if we really want to become the backbone of our civilization, then this is our responsibility.
The square pauses. Even students passing by come to a halt.
Then the applause comes, far more thunderous than anyone expected.
I've heard pieces of this before, but I never dug deeper. I need to look into it.
Sure, her background means she's got her own slant. But the guts it took to say all that? That alone deserves respect.
Give me the link to their newspaper.
But after this, will the TEC and Kurono really just let it slide...?
At the center of the gathered students, the girl gives them a single, deep bow, held for a long moment.
Thank you. Thank you for hearing me out.
In the walkway beside the square.
You were here before she even opened her mouth. Were you about to shut her down?
I tried. Didn't work. So now I'm just keeping watch.
Adelyde offers no reply, just presses her back against the column, arms folded tight. Her face is shadowed, and when she speaks, her voice is so low it almost does not carry.
I'm thinking about what she said.
Even if I wanted to change the family from within, I couldn't do it on my own. But the voices calling out the TEC and Kurono have never been loud enough to matter.
Kurono's shady experiments, the TEC's political purges... Aren't those enough to wake people up?
The TEC's money is right in front of them. Their fangs are somewhere off in the distance.

You really expect someone living grant to grant, putting their siblings through school, to turn on the people funding them? Or someone with a promising future to throw it away? That's not how the world works.
If I weren't a Helio, I'd have been the first to clap. But if I draw my family's attention to her now, I'd be putting her in the line of fire.
Too bad there are no ifs.

I'll be blunt, princess. Your background and your resources made you who you are. You can't hold onto all of that and still have the freedom to stand over there and clap. You don't get to have it both ways.
With a yawn, she raises a hand in a lazy wave and starts to move away.
And I'd watch the people around her. She's got guts, and others may not. The ones cheering today could be the ones selling her out tomorrow.
People buckle under pressure more easily than anything else. Who knows, right?
In the Tactics instructor's office, with a clear view of the square below.
I caught the whole thing. One of your students?
So much for that advice I gave you. Didn't take, I see.
But I respect what she did. And word is, the higher-ups at the academy have been eyeing the TEC's influence on F.O.S. for a while now, just waiting for the right trigger to start digging.
Then you should know the only thing keeping her safe inside these walls right now is the rulebook.
...You're not about to say you're going to protect her.
Wells smiles, adjusts his glasses, and taps his communication mic.
There's more. Why do you think I had you listen in too?
I've just handed you a situation that has no direct ties to World Government interests, and one you can move on without needing clearance.
Morning, Several Weeks Later, F.O.S. Campus Broadcast
Morning announcement. Earlier, a student delivered a public address at Prism Square, raising concerns regarding the partnership between the Transatlantic Economic Community and Kurono.

The World Government Committee on Scientific Ethics has conducted a preliminary review of the allegations. The committee reports that all route documentation is complete and compliant, with no evidence of violations found.
The Transatlantic Economic Community has issued a statement expressing regret over what it calls unfounded speculation and reaffirming its commitment to full transparency in any investigation.
That same day, we initiated a comprehensive compliance audit of all Transatlantic Economic Community funding and associated projects.

Seventeen projects have been ordered suspended pending review, including the technical co-sponsorship agreement for this year's Military Combat Competition, data-sharing clauses related to sponsored students, and seat assignments for three endowed research fund review panels.
We reiterate that F.O.S. will not accept funding that is deceptive or non-transparent in nature. This concludes the morning announcement.
Great Family Council, Transatlantic Economic Community.
We kept the government side quiet. No findings came through. But F.O.S. closed its doors. All seventeen projects are suspended.
The technical co-sponsorship for the competition is gone. The scholarship recipient lists are off-limits. Not a single panel seat left.
We spent three years planning this. Every military district officer was supposed to pass through our hands first.
And now Dominik's academy is combing through our donations line by line... Ma'am, the Helio family has put up just as much funding as the Erhorns, if not more.
That tall figure remains silent in the shadowed corner of the conference room.
As far as we can tell, she didn't even ask anyone to sign on with her.
She stands at last and moves toward the door. As she passes the projection, her gaze catches on the young face captured in the student activity corner.
